rows.title: Opening run follows the Design Release 2.1 step order and ends on the review page
rows.detail: A trader starting a new notification is carried through the pages in Design Release 2.1's order: the reason for import is asked straight after what is being imported and before commodity details, the CPH number page is no longer a step after roles and addresses (it is reached only from its row there), roles and addresses goes on to the contact address unless everything is already complete, and the contact address always goes on to the review page, which names anything still outstanding. The tests repo's full journey is rewritten as Design Release 2.1's cattle-by-air journey in the new order, because today's cattle-by-road walk follows the old order and would break.
acceptanceCriteria: In a new notification's opening run, 'Save and continue' on 'What are you importing?' goes to 'Main reason for import', and 'Save and continue' on 'Main reason for import' goes to 'Commodity details'. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:1495-1501; trace:prototype-dr2-1 index.json pages for both traces)

In the opening run, 'Save and continue' on 'Commodity details' goes to 'Identification details' when a chosen commodity needs animal identifiers, and otherwise to 'Additional details'. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 index.json pages for both traces)

In the opening run, 'Save and continue' on 'Roles and addresses' goes to 'Contact address for this consignment', including for a consignment that needs a CPH number; the run never shows the CPH number page. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:1523-1527, app/routes.js:1495-1534)

The CPH number page opens only from its row on 'Roles and addresses', and saving it returns to 'Roles and addresses'. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:1495-1534; repo:tests tests/animals/e2e/features/cph-scope.spec.ts:56-64)

When every section on the overview is already complete, 'Save and continue' on 'Roles and addresses' goes to the overview instead of the contact address page. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:1545-1547)

'Save and continue' on 'Contact address for this consignment' at the end of the opening run goes to the review page even when the notification is incomplete, and the review page names what is outstanding. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:1523-1527, app/routes.js:1536-1554; prototype:dr2-1-specs COVERAGE.md:163-164)

The tests repo walks a cattle-by-air notification from create to 'Import notification submitted' in this order: origin of the import with a region code and an internal reference, 'What are you importing?' with cattle (Bos taurus), 'Main reason for import' (Internal market, Breeding), 'Commodity details' for 2 animals, 'Identification details' with an ear tag and passport for each animal, 'Additional details' with the unweaned question answered, arrival details by air, transporter, documents, 'Roles and addresses' with a CPH number, contact address, review, declaration. (prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/journeys.fit.spec.js:222-236; trace:prototype-dr2-1 index.json pages for both traces)

In that walk, every task on the overview reads 'Complete' before the review is opened, and the review shows the origin with its region code, the internal reference, Bos taurus, Breeding, the purpose given, the CPH number and the chosen transporter. (prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/journeys.fit.spec.js:222-236, COVERAGE.md Behaviour worth knowing)

sources.ref: index.json pages for both traces (opening run order)

rows.gate: Look at the opening run end to end on a new notification: reason for import before commodity details, no CPH step, contact address then review even when incomplete. Every later row's end-to-end walk, in every area, follows this order.
rows.notes: Combines four thin slices that all change the opening run's step list and next-page rule (req-1610 reason before commodity details, c-202; req-1611 no CPH step, c-203; req-1612 complete-run skip; req-1614 run always ends on review, c-205) with req-1655, the tests repo's whole-journey proof, because the reorder breaks today's cattle-by-road walk and the same helper has to be rewritten in the same change. The frontend's own rule that a run with no open later step ends on the overview (repo-frontend-p1-113) still holds and is not overruled. The frontend's journey-flow documentation is updated to the new order in the same change. The unweaned question is asked for cattle today; req-175 (another area) widens it to pigs and does not block this walk.

rows.title: A page opened from an overview task returns to the overview on save
rows.detail: Every Design Release 2.1 overview task opens its page in an overview context, and that page goes back to the overview when the trader presses 'Save and continue'. Today several pages chain on through the rest of their section first. Each chained-to page has its own overview row, so nothing becomes unreachable.
acceptanceCriteria: Opened from its overview task, 'What are you importing?' goes to the overview on 'Save and continue', not to 'Commodity details'. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:1588-1602, app/routes.js:440-442)
Opened from its overview task, 'Main reason for import' goes to the overview on 'Save and continue', not to 'Additional details'. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:1588-1602)
Opened from its overview task, 'Arrival details' goes to the overview on 'Save and continue', not to 'Transit countries' or the transporter page. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:1588-1602)
Opened from its overview task, 'Roles and addresses' goes to the overview on 'Save and continue', not to the CPH number page. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:1588-1602)

'Commodity details', 'Additional details', 'Transit countries' and the transporter page each open from their own overview row and return to the overview on 'Save and continue'. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:1588-1602)
'Upload documents' opened from the overview keeps its add-another round trip on the page, then returns to the overview on 'Save and continue'. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:1588-1602)
rows.notes: One slice (req-1615, c-204): section chaining after the overview has been shown is removed for every section. Kept apart from the Back-link row because that one waits on template editing from another area. Depends on the opening-run step-order row (same flow code, and the tests that drive the overview follow the new order). Existing tests that rely on chaining (animal-identifiers-cap, reason-purpose-scope, the journey helper's completeAnswerSections) change with it.

rows.title: Back links follow the context a page was opened in
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 builds every journey page's Back link from how the page was reached: to the overview from an overview task, to the template's review page from a template review, and otherwise to the previous page in the step order, including when the page was opened from the review page's Change link. Today task pages point Back at the overview whatever context they were opened in.
acceptanceCriteria: A page opened from its overview task has a 'Back' link to the overview. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:488-498)

A page reached by 'Save and continue' in the opening run has a 'Back' link to the previous page in the step order: 'Main reason for import' goes back to 'What are you importing?', and 'Commodity details' goes back to 'Main reason for import'. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:488-498, app/routes.js:1495-1501)

A page opened from a Change link on the review page has a 'Back' link to the previous page in the step order, not to the review page; 'Save and continue' there still returns to the review page. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:488-498)
A page opened from a template's review page has a 'Back' link to that template's review page. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:488-498)
rows.notes: One slice (req-1616, c-206). Depends on the opening-run step-order row (the previous page is taken from the new order) and on the templates area's row that lets a template be edited from its review page (req-1358): the template-review criterion cannot be observed before that context exists, and a requirement cannot be split across rows. Pages behind 'Roles and addresses' (party pickers, CPH number) keep their Back link to it (repo-tests-p2-042), which is not a journey step.

rows.title: 'Save and return to overview' saves without the page's required-answer checks
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader leave most pages for the overview without finishing them, so they can come back later. The backend already stores missing or empty answers. An answer that breaks its own format rule is still refused, because the service cannot store a value that does not fit its field, and consignment details and the contact address page keep checking their answers before saving, as Design Release 2.1 does.
acceptanceCriteria: On origin of the import, 'What are you importing?', 'Main reason for import', 'Identification details', 'Additional details', 'Arrival details', 'Transit countries', the transporter page, 'Upload documents' and 'Roles and addresses', pressing 'Save and return to overview' with a required answer missing shows no error, saves what was entered and goes to the overview. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:1560-1566; prototype:dr2-1-specs COVERAGE.md:158)
After such a save the page's overview task does not read 'Complete', and reopening the page shows the answers that were entered. (prototype:dr2-1-specs COVERAGE.md:163-164)

An answer that fails its own format rule, such as an impossible arrival date or a malformed region code, is refused on 'Save and return to overview' with that answer's error, and the page is not saved. (ruling:sam-2026-10-07 claim 10)

On 'Commodity details' and 'Contact address for this consignment', 'Save and return to overview' with a required answer missing shows the page's errors and saves nothing. (prototype:dr2-1-specs COVERAGE.md:162)

sources.ref: app/routes.js:1560-1566 (hub and review are soft-save actions)
claim 10 (validation and persistence override the prototype)
p1-026, p1-073, p1-098, p1-100, p1-112 (missing and empty answers stored)

rows.gate: Look at one soft-save page and one format-refused answer: the pattern for leaving a page unfinished is set here, and other areas' per-page 'Save and return to overview' rows follow it.
rows.notes: One slice (req-1625, c-211), kept apart because it changes the exit rule shared by every page. Other areas carry page-level versions of the same rule (req-088 commodity page, req-166 main import reason, req-180 additional details, req-329 arrival and transit, req-540 upload documents); the combiner should merge those into this row where they repeat the same set-up. The CPH number page outside amend ends with 'Save and continue' alone (req-605), so it has no 'Save and return to overview' to test. No backend change is expected: the backend already stores missing or empty answers.

rows.title: Hard stops: means of transport on arrival details and number of packages on commodity details
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 makes the means of transport the only hard stop on 'Arrival details', because it decides whether transit countries apply; the other arrival answers can be left for later. On commodity details the number of packages becomes a hard stop, alongside the number of animals, on each line that asks for it.
acceptanceCriteria: On 'Arrival details', 'Save and continue' with no means of transport chosen is refused with an error on the means of transport question. (prototype:dr2-1-specs COVERAGE.md:162)

On 'Arrival details', 'Save and continue' with a means of transport chosen and the arrival date, port of entry, transport identification and transport document reference blank goes on to the next page. (prototype:dr2-1-specs COVERAGE.md:158)

On 'Commodity details', 'Save and continue' with a line that asks for a number of packages left without one is refused with an error on that line's number of packages. (prototype:dr2-1-specs COVERAGE.md:162)

On 'Commodity details', a line that does not ask for a number of packages can be saved without one. (prototype:dr2-1-specs COVERAGE.md:162; repo:frontend src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/lines.js:4-8)
rows.notes: Combines two hard-stop slices (req-1642 arrival, req-1643 packages): both change which answers are required to proceed, on the obligations rather than the page content, and are reviewed together. The error wording for each new hard stop is taken from the Design Release 2.1 page and kept as its own criterion in the plan. Which species ask for a number of packages is req-112 (another area); this row only makes the question required where it is asked. Existing tests that say arrival details is enforced as a whole page (transit-means-scope) change with it.

rows.title: Page endings: 'hub' wording on the contact address page, and the amend ending on pages reached from roles and addresses
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 words the contact address page's return controls with 'hub'. While a notification is being amended, the party pickers, the CPH number page and the permanent address page gain the amend-only 'Save and return' (to the review page) and 'Save and continue' buttons, and keep the hub control off, as DR1 ruled for pages reached from another page. Outside amend they keep the primary button alone.
acceptanceCriteria: The contact address for consignment page's return controls read 'Save and return to hub' and 'Cancel and return to hub'. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace pet-cats-by-air actions 100-150, trace poultry-by-rail action 133)

While a notification is being amended, each party picker (place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination) ends with a primary 'Save and return' button and a secondary 'Save and continue' button, and no 'Save and return to overview'. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/partials/design-release-2.1/journey-form-actions.html:7-10, 44-56, 88-96; document:dr1-parity-notes rule (b))

While a notification is being amended, the CPH number page and the permanent address page end with a primary 'Save and return' button and a secondary 'Save and continue' button, and no 'Save and return to overview'. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/partials/design-release-2.1/journey-form-actions.html:7-10; document:dr1-parity-notes rule (b))

On those pages while amending, 'Save and return' saves and goes to the review page, and 'Save and continue' saves and goes to 'Roles and addresses'. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/partials/design-release-2.1/journey-form-actions.html:44-56)
Outside amend, the party pickers, the CPH number page and the permanent address page still end with the primary 'Save and continue' button alone. (document:dr1-parity-notes rule (b))

sources.ref: rule (b): a page reached from another page ends with the primary button alone

rows.notes: Combines two ending slices on the shared journey buttons (req-1622, c-209; req-1624, c-210): both change which controls a page ends with, in the same shared partial. Depends on the row that builds the permanent address as its own page (req-727, another area), since one criterion is about that page. req-770 (another area) says the same amend ending for the contact, CPH and permanent address pages: the combiner should merge it into this row. Welsh versions of the changed strings follow req-725 (another area).

rows.title: End-to-end proof: horse by sea under temporary admission
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 proves a horse-by-sea journey end to end. The real journey already offers horses and the temporary admission reason, but no end-to-end test walks them.
acceptanceCriteria: The tests repo walks a horse-by-sea notification from create to 'Import notification submitted': origin Republic of Ireland, one horse (Equus caballus), 'Temporary admission horses' with an exit date and a port of exit, microchip, passport and horse name, 'Registered equine animal', arrival by sea with a transport identification, and a transporter. (prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/journeys.fit.spec.js:277-290)
In that walk, every task on the overview reads 'Complete' before the review is opened. (prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/journeys.fit.spec.js:277-290)
The review shows 'Temporary admission horses', the port of exit, 'Registered equine animal' and the chosen transporter. (prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/journeys.fit.spec.js:277-290)
rows.notes: One slice (req-1658). Tests only, because the frontend already supports every answer this walk gives (repo-frontend-p2-026, p2-086, p2-100). Depends on the opening-run step-order row, whose rewritten journey helper this walk uses.

rows.title: End-to-end proof: poultry by rail in transit
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 proves a poultry-by-rail journey end to end, with transit countries and no identification step. Today poultry cannot be chosen; the commodities area adds Chicken to the catalogue, and this row proves the whole journey with it.
acceptanceCriteria: The tests repo walks a poultry-by-rail notification from create to 'Import notification submitted': origin Germany, Chicken (010511) Gallus domesticus, 'Transit' with an exit port and the Republic of Ireland as destination country, arrival by rail with a transport identification, transit through Belgium and France, a transporter and a CPH number. (prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/journeys.fit.spec.js:237-250; trace:prototype-dr2-1 poultry-by-rail)
In that walk no 'Identification details' page is shown and the overview has no 'Identification details' task. (prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/journeys.fit.spec.js:237-250)

In that walk, every task on the overview reads 'Complete' before the review is opened, and the review shows Germany, Transit, Belgium and the chosen transporter. (prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/journeys.fit.spec.js:237-250)
rows.notes: One slice (req-1656). Depends on the commodities area's row that adds Chicken (010511) to the catalogue (req-094) and on the opening-run step-order row. Drafted tests-only because the frontend change it needs is that other row's; the combiner should fold this criterion set into req-094's row as its end-to-end proof, which makes it a full-stack slice and removes the cross-area dependency.

rows.title: End-to-end proof: pet cats by air with permanent addresses
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 proves a pet-cats-by-air journey end to end, with each cat's permanent address chosen on its own page in roles and addresses. Conflict c-119 settles that the permanent address page is built now; this row proves the whole journey with it.
acceptanceCriteria: The tests repo walks a pet-cats-by-air notification from create to 'Import notification submitted': origin Spain, 2 cats (Felis catus), 'Internal market' as a companion animal not for resale or rehoming, a microchip, passport and tattoo for each cat, arrival by air, and a transporter. (prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/journeys.fit.spec.js:251-276)

In that walk, each cat's permanent address is chosen on the permanent address page reached from 'Roles and addresses': one 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' and one entered as a new address. (prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/journeys.fit.spec.js:251-276; trace:prototype-dr2-1 pet-cats-by-air)

In that walk, every task on the overview reads 'Complete' before the review is opened, and the review shows Spain, 'Companion animal not for resale or rehoming', Felis catus and the new address's first line. (prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/journeys.fit.spec.js:251-276)
rows.notes: One slice (req-1657, c-119). Depends on the rows that build the permanent address as its own page with the same-as-destination choice (req-727, req-746 and their area) and remove it from the identification form (req-263), and on the opening-run step-order row. Drafted tests-only because the frontend change it needs is those rows'; the combiner should fold this criterion set into the permanent address row as its end-to-end proof. Today's animal-identifiers-conditional test of the in-form permanent address is replaced by that row, not this one.
